title: Product of Array Except Self
prompt:
Given an array nums, return an array answer where answer[i] is the product of every element of nums except nums[i]. You must not use division, and it should run in O(n).

Write productExceptSelf(nums).

  • productExceptSelf([1, 2, 3, 4]) → [24, 12, 8, 6]
  • productExceptSelf([-1, 1, 0, -3, 3]) → [0, 0, 9, 0, 0]
  • productExceptSelf([5]) → [1] (the product of nothing is 1)

Constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 10^5, values may be negative or zero. (Tests treat -0 and 0 as equal.)

tests.name: one zero: only its own position is non-zero

hints: Trigger: "everything except i" plus "no division" plus O(n). Split it: everything to the left of i times everything to the right of i.
Idea: both halves are running products. Sweep left to right carrying the product of what you have passed; then sweep right to left doing the same for the right side.

Code shape: let left = 1; for (i = 0 → n-1) { answer[i] = left; left *= nums[i]; } then let right = 1; for (i = n-1 → 0) { answer[i] *= right; right *= nums[i]; }. Store before multiplying in, so position i never includes itself.
explain:
Time O(n): two passes. Space O(1) extra beyond the output array (just two running variables). The brute force was O(n²) because every position re-multiplied the same left and right stretches; the running products compute each stretch once.

Division would be O(n) too, but it breaks on zeros (and interviewers always test a zero). The left/right sweep is the general pattern behind many "for each position, something about everything before and after it" problems, like Trapping Rain Water (max to the left and right).

How to say it: "Product except self is left product times right product. I fill the answer with running products from the left, then multiply in running products from the right. Two passes, O(n) time, O(1) extra space, no division so zeros are fine."
